info.name: Bifrost V1 - Time-of-Day Pricing
info.description:
Regression coverage for peak/off-peak time-of-day pricing (off_peak_cost_multiplier + peak_hours on a model pricing row).

Each case creates a virtual-key-scoped pricing override that pins the token rates AND the schedule in the same patch, so the expected cost is fully determined by the override and never by whatever the live datasheet happens to say. That also means the assertions do not care how many tokens the provider actually returns: each run is checked against its own logged token counts.

Schedules are built relative to the run's own clock in a prerequest script, so no clock control is needed and the suite is correct at any hour or weekday. Every window lists all seven days, which keeps a window that wraps past midnight matching correctly.

Three invariants: a window containing the request bills at full rate; a window excluding it scales usage charges by the multiplier; a schedule that cannot be evaluated fails closed to peak. The third matters most, because base rates are the peak prices and an inverted fallback would silently under-bill every customer.

Runs against a gateway with management auth disabled, or with it enabled by passing admin_auth_header (newman --env-var admin_auth_header='Bearer <key>', or BIFROST_ADMIN_AUTH_HEADER for the runner script). That header is applied to /api/ calls only, never to the inference calls, which authenticate as the virtual key.

Deliberately does NOT set x-bf-expect-cost. The dbverify reporter recomputes expected cost from the datasheet and does not model the off-peak multiplier, so it would report the off-peak case as INACCURATE. These cases assert against the logs API themselves.

exec: // Management calls need admin auth when the gateway runs with it enabled.
// Deliberately scoped to /api/ paths: the inference calls authenticate as
// the virtual key via x-bf-vk, and upserting an admin Authorization header
// onto those would change which credential the request is billed under,
// which is the whole thing these cases are asserting on.

item.name: Setup - Peak override covering now (openai gpt-4o-mini)
item.description: Pins the rates and a peak window that contains the current instant. The multiplier is present but must not fire.

exec: // Build an HH:MM offset from now, in UTC. All windows below list every
// weekday, so a window that wraps past midnight still matches and the cases
// stay correct no matter which hour or day the suite runs at.
// A four-hour window centred on now, so the request lands well inside it
// even if the suite is slow.
var peakHours = { timezone: 'UTC', windows: [{ days: ALL_DAYS, start: hhmmFromNow(-2), end: hhmmFromNow(2) }] };
// Pinned so a datasheet flat fee cannot leak into the expected total.
// A flat per-request fee is deliberately not discounted off-peak, so
// leaving it unset would make the off-peak assertion depend on whether
// the live datasheet happens to carry one for this model.
// Virtual-key scoped on purpose. A global or provider-scoped override
// would halve the cost of every other request in flight and make the
// dbverify cost-accuracy checks in the rest of the suite report
// INACCURATE for reasons that have nothing to do with those cases.
pm.test('Setup - Peak override covering now (openai gpt-4o-mini) returns 2xx', function () { pm.expect(code, 'body: ' + pm.response.text()).to.be.within(200, 299); });
try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { body = null; }
